mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter financial conditions compressing equity discount rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month preceding the prediction window
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when the trigger occurs (t-test p > 0.05), or Fed Funds Rate does not exceed 4.0% in any month during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market weakness reduces consumer and business confidence, depressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 in the month preceding the prediction window
failure_condition: Over a 6-month rolling window, 60-day forward returns remain positive when the trigger is met (t-test p < 0.05), or unemployment claims do not exceed 200,000 in any month during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a bottom in supply-side softness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months, then rises above the prior trough in the third month
failure_condition: The pattern repeats but is followed by continued negative 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05), or the rebound is not accompanied by a positive forward return.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is negative as the surprise inflation erodes equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.5% surprise (current month vs prior month)
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the CPIAUCSL surprise > +0.5% is never followed by a statistically significant negative 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and supporting equity valuations, resulting in a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The three-month UNRATE trend persists but is followed by negative 20-day forward returns (t-test p < 0.05), or the Fed raises rates during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly surge in both HOUST and INDPRO above their 12-month moving averages suggests a bottom in economic activity and a rebound in consumer and business demand, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
Note: Since HOUST and INDPRO are the closest proxies for demand indicators in the catalog, this sketch demonstrates an interaction-driven mechanism using available proxies.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and INDPRO exceed their respective 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: The co-move persists but is not followed by a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05), or the proxies move together without any change in SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly personal earnings growth (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction) below -0.2% for two consecutive months, followed by a positive monthly revision, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a turning point in wage growth dynamics.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -0.2% for two consecutive months, then a positive revision in the following month
failure_condition: The wage growth pattern recurs but is not followed by a positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05), or the revision does not occur.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL) but stable or rising real GDP momentum (implied by INDPRO), a sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 5.0% for two months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate higher real interest rates and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5.0% for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL is flat or declining over the same horizon
regime_hint: High inflation containment with rising rates
failure_condition: The pattern recurs but is not followed by a negative 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.0% during the window.
